text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Historians to analyze Forces: Defence Minister Doug Young asks academics for ideas on how to improve military leadership structure.
- Kim Campbell's advisers briefed, note says: Ex-PM attacks Somalia report.
- Agreement reached on Hebron: Netanyahu's cabinet divided on deal; Arafat likely to face less opposition.
- Yeltsin infirmity triggers political crisis: Lower house of Russian parliament weighs steps to force President's resignation.
- Theft charges withdrawn as $12,000 donated: Gift to Ryerson from Toronto company raises questions about alternatives to criminal prosecution.
- Placer Dome makes grab for Bre-X: C$6.2-billion merger proposal aims to spark bidding war for firm and its giant gold find.
- Jusuf Merukh sues for slice of Busang.
- Canadian Pacific hangs on to Laidlaw now that prospects improving: Largest shareholder's stake has grown to about C$900-million.
- Gold goes south while TSE, Dow set records.
- Placer Dome woos Bre-X with C$6.4-billion merger: All-share offer would give Indonesia a 40-percent stake in Busang and make Bre-X president David Walsh Placer's biggest single shareholder.
- Gravis investors vow fight even after takeover is approved.
